steps.visual_purpose: Show the OrderInput BaseModel subclass beside the handler signature, with annotations identifying the customer identifier as path input, the ordinary scalar option as query input and body: OrderInput as structured JSON body input.

Show acquisition, yield, operation use, handler completion, response sending, and cleanup as separate events. Contrast default request scope with function scope, including successful and exceptional paths and re-raising an unhandled exception.

Show the order failure's unexplained 'failed' output beside the structured output, with timestamp, code location, event type, severity, result status and reason visibly labeled. Connect the extra dictionary's keys to the fields preserved by the formatter.

Make the outbound trust boundary visible across three separate stages: requested provider mapped to an allowed destination, the resolved address actually used for the connection, and any redirect target. Mark private, loopback, link-local and other non-public IPv4 and IPv6 destinations as forbidden for public-only access, and show where each stage requires enforcement.

Make the total-body middleware boundary, pre-binding multipart parser limits, typed metadata and file parameters, validation-before-processing order, and finally-based asynchronous file cleanup visible in one endpoint scaffold.

Make the CORSMiddleware declaration visible with annotations linking each explicit list and the credential flag to the shop client's requirements, alongside a separate boundary showing that browser access permission does not replace endpoint access checks.

Show separate boundaries for requests A and B. Within each boundary, trace one provider execution supplying the same instance to two dependants. Contrast a declaration using use_cache=False, which requires a fresh execution rather than reuse of the cached result.
Make the TestClient context, GET request, status assertion, and JSON assertion visible together, alongside the pytest result for the synthetic order-retrieval contract.

tiles.title: Declare and inspect an input contract

steps.visual_purpose: Show rows for omitted note, explicit null and a concrete string, with columns comparing acceptance and resulting value for note: str | None versus note: str | None = None. Keep presence requirements and admitted values separately visible.

Make the POST /orders method entry and both schema references visible alongside components.schemas.OrderInput and components.schemas.OrderOutput, showing quantity as the input field and id as the output field.

Make the host boundary visible by pairing an allowlist configuration with supplied Host values and outcomes: accepted, rejected with 400, or redirected when an applicable www_redirect policy is enabled. Distinguish exact-domain, subdomain-wildcard, and all-host-wildcard policies.

Make the synthetic failure inputs and resulting emitted record visible together, showing removal or masking of the fake token and connection-string secret in both message and supplemental context while retaining the intended event field.

Show one engine-bound session_factory supplying separate session A and session B boxes for concurrent requests. Trace each session through dependency yield to context exit, with normal and exceptional paths both ending in cleanup.

Make the shutdown sequence visible: an active order request, termination initiation, old processes stopping acceptance of new connections, bounded completion of active responses and background tasks, and lifespan resource cleanup. Mark the configured wait boundary and show the recorded response outcome and shared-client closure evidence.

Show separate liveness and readiness decision paths: HTTP statuses 200–399 count as success; failures reaching the configured threshold lead respectively to possible container restart or removal of traffic eligibility. Include a temporary required-backend outage with the process still alive to make the readiness-only effect visible.
